name: spindoctor-qwerty
description: SpinDoctor 3.1.2 quantum-circuit SIMULATOR for Claude Desktop: q.* scripts, 241 presets, q.folder, theory tests, TXT/PDF reports. Classical, not a quantum computer.
long_description:
SpinDoctor Qwerty 1.1.0 runs the SpinDoctor 3.1.2 quantum-circuit simulator on your computer as a local MCP server for Claude Desktop.

- Six tools: function table, run q.* scripts, run any of the 241 presets, list presets, read reports, and test a theory (from a file, pasted text, or a summary of the chat you confirm).
- 1-298 logical qubits per register, 59 per entangled factor; registers wider than 29 qubits sample in basis z only.
- q.folder runs a folder of .txt/.csv/.json/.qasm/.qasm2/.circuit/.pdf command files (top level, up to 128 files).
- Every command writes TXT and PDF reports (plus JSON and CSV) into the workspace folder you choose.

Honest limits: this is a classical FP64 simulation. It is not a quantum computer and gives no quantum speed-up or advantage. Memory grows as 2^n x 16 bytes for an entangled n-qubit block. Needs Python 3.8 or newer (standard library only; NumPy optional); nothing is downloaded or installed.

tools.name: spindoctor_run_script
tools.description: Run SpinDoctor q.* commands (one per line); returns results and TXT/PDF/JSON/CSV report paths

tools.name: spindoctor_run_preset
tools.description: Run one of the 241 SpinDoctor presets (qc-001..qc-241) with optional overrides

tools.name: spindoctor_list_presets
tools.description: List or filter the 241 SpinDoctor presets

tools.name: spindoctor_report
tools.description: List or read SpinDoctor reports in the workspace

tools.name: spindoctor_functions
tools.description: Show every SpinDoctor function as a Markdown table (Function | What it does | Command to type)

tools.name: spindoctor_test_theory
tools.description: Test a theory from a file, pasted text or a confirmed chat summary with quoted excerpts; writes a TXT/PDF theory test report

workspace.title: SpinDoctor workspace
workspace.description: Folder for SpinDoctor state and its TXT/PDF/JSON/CSV reports. Theory files you want tested can be anywhere on this computer.
